[30]   Its topography features a diverse landscape shaped by geological processes, including low rolling hills in the east and south, contrasted with rugged mountains and uplands in the north and west.  [31]   The island measures approximately 1,000 kilometers from north to south and up to 500 kilometers east to west at its broadest, with a heavily indented coastline exceeding 10,000 kilometers in length due to fjords, bays, and estuaries.  [31]   In northern Scotland, the Scottish Highlands dominate with ancient, eroded mountains, including the Grampian range where Ben Nevis rises to 1,345 meters, the highest point on the island.  [32]   South of the Highlands lies the Central Lowlands , a fertile valley belt flanked by the Southern Uplands , which transition into the hilly terrain of northern England , marked by the Pennine Chain—a spine of uplands reaching elevations around 800 meters.  [31]   Wales, to the west, presents a compact mountainous interior, with Snowdonia's Yr Wyddfa ( Snowdon ) at 1,085 meters as its peak, alongside deep valleys and plateaus.  [33]   Central and southern England consist primarily of lowland plains and undulating downs, such as the English Lowlands and Weald , interspersed with isolated uplands like the Lake District —home to Scafell Pike at 978 meters—and the Peak District .  [33]   Major rivers, including the Severn (354 kilometers, the longest), Thames (346 kilometers), and Trent, drain these regions eastward to the North Sea or westward to the Irish Sea and Atlantic, shaping fertile floodplains and supporting extensive agriculture.

# Fjord Defence Group (DFENS) Q3 2026 earnings summary

Event summary combining transcript, slides, and related documents.

## Q3 2026 earnings summary

26 Nov, 2026

### Executive summary

- Q3 Pro Forma Defence revenue was NOK 240.1m, up 20% YoY, with EBITDA of NOK 46.4m and a 19.3% margin.
- Q3 IFRS revenue was NOK 157.3m; adjusted EBITDA was NOK 33.2m before transaction costs, and EBIT was NOK -25.3m after NOK 31.6m of amortisation.
- Defence order backlog reached NOK 1.7bn at 30 September; PartnerTech closed on 26 August, expanding precision manufacturing capacity.
- 2026 targets remain above NOK 1bn Pro Forma Defence revenue and NOK 190–205m EBITDA; 2027 guidance is NOK 1.2–1.4bn revenue and NOK 230–250m EBITDA.

### Financial highlights

- Pro Forma Defence revenue was NOK 240.1m in Q3 2026 versus NOK 200.7m in Q3 2025; EBITDA was NOK 46.4m versus NOK 50.4m.
- Q3 IFRS revenue was NOK 157.3m versus NOK 17.0m YoY; adjusted EBITDA was NOK 33.2m versus NOK -4.7m before transaction costs.
- Q3 net loss was NOK 59.7m versus NOK 36.9m; YTD revenue was NOK 245.8m and net loss NOK 149.0m.
- YTD adjusted EBITDA was NOK 40.1m; transaction costs were NOK 42.8m, including NOK 21.4m in Q3.
- LTM Pro Forma Defence revenue was NOK 976.7m and EBITDA NOK 184.3m, at an 18.9% margin.

### Outlook and guidance

- 2026 Pro Forma Defence targets remain revenue above NOK 1bn and EBITDA of NOK 190–205m; remaining-year volume is supported by firm orders.
- 2027 guidance is NOK 1.2–1.4bn Defence revenue and NOK 230–250m EBITDA; ~70% is covered by firm orderbook and confirmed call-offs.
- 2027 guidance assumes current structure and scheduled delivery under existing contracts and framework agreements; it excludes potential M&A.
- 2029 Defence EBITDA ambition is NOK 400–500m from organic growth and smaller bolt-ons; EPS is targeted to grow faster than underlying EBITDA.
